scoring_justification: Melting temperature can be recomputed from the agent's raw TE-Hp curve by averaging over the coexistence plateau; compared to paper-reported value with tolerance. Curve shape and Q6 profile are structural audits.

hidden_assets.purpose: Hidden reference melting temperature of Cu from modified void method
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper text: 'the calculated melting temperature ... is ~1327 ± 14 K at ambient pressure' (Section 3.5, Fig. 9).
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: Paper-reported central result, used as gold for threshold comparison.

outputs.description: CSV output of the TE-Hp scan for Cu from NPH simulations; checker verifies three-regime shape.
Melting temperature (in Kelvin) for Cu averaged over the coexistence plateau; compared to paper-reported gold with tolerance.
Q6 order parameter profile along Z for Cu; checker confirms coexistence through distinct solid/liquid Q6 values.

output_contract.notes: All outputs must be placed under /app/outputs. The melting temperature is the headline result; the TE-Hp curve and Q6 profile provide supporting structural evidence.

steps.description: Verify TE-Hp curve shape: three regimes (solid, coexistence, liquid), monotonicity, plateau flatness.
Verify Q6 profile shows coexistence: solid-like (Q6 > 0.45) and liquid-like (Q6 < 0.40) regions.
